items.title: Claude Code 2.1.318 released
items.text: Added a record of your answer when Claude Code asks to turn on the mods it writes in a session · Added assume_role on mantle upstreams of the Claude apps gateway, for a role in another AWS account and for per-developer AWS cost attribution · Added an effort option to a mod's $.model.fork, so a quick side job can run at low whatever effort the session uses; the result reports the effort sent · Added the date a stored claude.ai sign-in ends to claude auth status (loginExpiresAt) and to claude -p JSON results (credential_expires_at)

items.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
items.text: Yesterday's hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper (OK, the authors classify is as a "blog post", but it's paper-shaped) found that frontier models, in particular GPT-6 Astra, can both interpret and modify the raw weights of a machine learning model - literally a text description of the model containing a bunch of floating point numbers.
